newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia needs rate cut to boost jobs - Opp'n.
newsitem.headline: Australia needs rate cut to boost jobs - Opp'n.

text.p: Australia's Labor opposition on Friday urged the Reserve Bank of Australia to cut official cash rates again -- for the fifth time in a year -- to help combat chronic unemployment.

Opposition treasury spokesman Gareth Evans said the government should also cancel some spending cuts, boost exports, develop industry and regional strategies, boost education funding and create community service jobs.

"With over 40,000 jobs lost in May ... unemployment now at 8.8 percent, and the trend in job growth now negative -- can anyone now believe this government is on the right track?" Evans wrote in the Sydney-based Daily Telegraph.
"The Reserve Bank can help with interest rate cuts, but the government has to change budget direction as well."
Evans said the conservative Liberal-National government should abandon some of the massive spending cuts in the last two budgets aimed at restoring government finances to a surplus.
"It's not as if we had to have massive budget cuts. Our budget deficit and public debt were both at levels ... that the Western Europeans, for starters, would die for," Evans said.

The government has projected its underlying budget -- which excludes windfalls such as asset sales -- to turn into a A$1.6 billion surplus in 1998/99 from a A$6.9 billion deficit in its first budget, for 1996/97, after cutting spending by billions of dollars.
Unemployment has failed to fall below 8.5 percent since the coalition won the election that ended 13 years of Labor rule in March 1996, and was 8.8 percent in May.
